## Description

Something wrong with how we handle `()`, these are clearly a punctuation, and should not be part of formalization, naturalization and translation.

I didn't find any definitions of "lies on" in Wikipedia, Wikidata, Wiktionary, so here we should try to expand on our API sources, if these are accessible from the browser.

The source text I took from California article on Wikipedia, so it means wiki projects have missing data to fully formalize all its texts.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_coast does not have translation to the Russian, but as we have it in English, we can try recursively translate the article itself using our translation algorithm, recursive article translation should be experimental feature, that is disabled by default. We must also have dedicated UI for the entire Wikipedia article translation. And we also need to have overrides here.

Recheck my findings. Also we need to form a clear instructions and guides on how to contribute missing data for wiki projects manually and using dedicated scripts, so we give account credentials and be able to contribute missing data change/edit.

```
### User
lies on

### AI
The phrase **"lies on"** generally means to rest atop a surface or to be located on a specific line or boundary. However, the exact meaning depends on the context:

* **Geography/Location:** Something is situated on or along a border, feature, or route (e.g., *“The town **lies on** the riverbank.”*)
* **Math/Geometry:** A point is located along a line, axis, or plane (e.g., *“The coordinate (x,y) **lies on** the x-axis.”*)
* **Responsibility:** The duty or burden falls upon someone (e.g., *“The decision **lies on** your shoulders.”*)

If you had a specific phrase or question in mind, please provide more details!

***

### User
"lies on" give me sources, where definition is described in

### AI
The definition of **"lies on"** (or the base phrasal verb **"lie on/upon"**) varies depending on the dictionary resource. 

#### Dictionary Sources & Definitions

* **Merriam-Webster:** Defines **"lie on/upon"** as a phrasal verb meaning **to affect someone in a specified way**. 
  * *Example:* "Guilt **lies on** his conscience."
  * *Source:* View the [Merriam-Webster Dictionary entry](https://merriam-webster.com).
* **Collins English Dictionary:** Highlights the use of "lie" followed by "on" or "upon" to mean **to rest, press, or weigh heavily** on something, such as a person's mind or thoughts. It also covers physical placement (e.g., "the pencil is **lying on** the desk").
  * *Example:* "My sins **lie** heavily **on** my mind."
  * *Source:* Check the [Collins Dictionary definition](https://collinsdictionary.com).
* **Oxford Learner's Dictionaries:** Describes "lie" combined with adverbs/prepositions like "on" to indicate being **located in a particular place** or staying flat on a surface.
  * *Example:* "The town **lies on** the coast."
  * *Source:* Browse the [Oxford Learner's Dictionary description](https://oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com).
* **The Free Dictionary (Webster's 1913):** Lists two traditional definitions for **"To lie on"**: (a) **To depend on** (e.g., *his life lies on the result*), and (b) **To bear, rest, press, or weigh on**.
  * *Source:* See the [Free Dictionary archive](https://freedictionary.org).
```

We also need to enhance our verb phrases detection, so for example we don't treat `lies on` as lies and on separately, as these have all completely different meanings.

We need to make sure access to all external APIs is unified via links notation, so we do requests to sources and get JSON, but as the result we should get links notation unification, where all fields with the same meaning will have exactly the same name.

We also need to give ability while keeping originals in cache query the data using links, in such a way, that we are able to access meanings collection, words, noun phrases, verb phrases and so on for all linguistic categories, so all the data collected from different sources is merged in unified virtual links view, so we can do query it from any required angle. And on top of this unified view of data, we should be able to add smart overrides, if data is missing in all sources, we can add these on top of virtual view, and later we will be able contribute all the data to all the sources, buy until changes are applied our system can function fully and correctly. We must ensure all our logic does not use direct access to any specific source but all access is done via virtualized and overridable view. When we do access to virtual view it should trigger loading all relevant data to satisfy the request to the cache (originals), and if data is missing we can use overrides (links notation on top of virtual view). We should not do overrides on top of external API, only use our abstraction. Yet, our abstraction should hide or remove any data, meaning anything that was accessible via external APIs should also be acccessible via our virtual links/links notation views.

Use https://gist.githubusercontent.com/konard/bf05b6fbb675ee2d80655aca854c49c4/raw/59226c26cf3b06107a2cf147799040fab12c0cb2/translation-debug-log.txt for all details on how it worked, check for any other clear errors in this log, and all other translations, that we are doing wrong and have the same mistakes.

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis 
(also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
